name: Japan
tagline: A named minority route, on a calendar built for the people using it
summary: Japan's English-taught bachelor's degrees are not a feature of the Japanese system; they are a deliberate, named, countable set built on top of it over the last fifteen years, and the IB Diploma is one of the qualifications they were designed to receive. The University of Tokyo's PEAK closed after September 2026, and Todai replaced it with something larger — the UTokyo College of Design, a new English-taught faculty opening in September 2027 whose international route names the IB Diploma first. Around it sit Waseda's six English-based schools, Keio's PEARL and GIGA, Sophia's Faculty of Liberal Arts, ICU, Tohoku's Future Global Leadership, Kyoto's iUP, APU and Akita. The calendar is the thing to understand before anything else: the Japanese academic year runs April to March and most students enter in April, so the September intake exists largely for international applicants — which is exactly why it fits a May 2027 IB session, and why its deadlines run from October 2026 to April 2027, every one of them before results.
whyConsider: The University of Tokyo opens its first new undergraduate faculty in about seventy years in September 2027, taught entirely in English, with half its hundred places on a route built for international qualifications and the IB named first.

Keio's PEARL runs three application periods for September 2027 entry, the last closing on 7 April 2027 and deciding on 24 May — the latest Japanese deadline we found, and the only one that lands after the examination session.
Waseda takes one application for six English-based schools in a single winter window, which is unusually friendly against Japan's older October deadlines.

Kyoto's iUP asks for no Japanese at all: six months of intensive preparatory language teaching, then four years of undergraduate study, with admission and tuition fee waivers and monthly scholarships.
MEXT's undergraduate scholarship is genuinely large — five years, 117,000 yen a month, all fees waived and airfare both ways in the 2027 round — provided you are willing to study in Japanese.
Several programmes, ICU and Akita and APU among them, are built on a bilingual liberal-arts model that maps onto the Diploma's breadth better than most European first degrees do.
watchOuts: PEAK has ended, and that is not the same as Todai closing. The College of Design's applications for September 2027 closed on 5 November 2026, the earliest Japanese deadline recorded here, and it is a five-year integrated bachelor's and master's programme rather than a bachelor's degree.

April is the default intake and September is the exception. April 2027 entry would have meant applying in the middle of 2026 and is not realistic for this cohort; Kyoto's iUP enrols in October, which is a third calendar again.
There is no central portal, no shared calendar and no common application. Six months separate the earliest deadline from the latest, and each application carries its own fee.

MEXT is not a route into the English-taught sector. The undergraduate scholarship funds a preparatory year in Japanese followed by a degree taught in Japanese; English-medium study happens only through 'direct placement', which MEXT decides, and MEXT also chooses the university, with no objection allowed.

The MEXT window for an April 2028 arrival falls in April and May 2027, on top of the IB examinations, and the exact Danish dates belong to the Embassy of Japan in Copenhagen — whose own web pages refused every request when this was researched. That gap is real and is recorded as one.

Only one institution's fees were read from an official page in this pass and the page carries no price year. The fee table linked from Japan's official study-promotion site is drawn from the Student Guide to Japan 2019–2020.

Japanese universities generally want documents apostilled and sometimes notarised, and a Certificate of Eligibility must be obtained before the student visa. Neither fits inside a November deadline arranged in October.

ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: There is no national rule to find. A full IB Diploma satisfies the twelve-years-of-schooling condition that Japanese universities apply to foreign applicants, and each programme then sets its own standard on top. The University of Tokyo's College of Design lists the IB Diploma first among the qualifications its Route B accepts, alongside the Abitur, the Baccalauréat, GCE and International A-levels and the European Baccalaureate; Keio's PEARL accepts an IB Diploma or predicted grades. Whether any programme publishes a minimum point score was not established in this pass.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: No national conversion table. Each programme reads IB points directly.
notes: Predicted grades do the work. Every September 2027 decision recorded here is made before 6 July 2027, the earliest of them four and a half months before, and Keio says in as many words that predictions are acceptable.

Some programmes want SAT or ACT, or the Examination for Japanese University Admission for International Students, on top of the IB. The requirements are not uniform and have to be read programme by programme.

MEXT's scholarship route applies its own academic condition — twelve years of schooling completed by March of the arrival year, or by August where the applicant enters in the autumn term through direct placement. A Danish gymnasium finishing in June sits between the two, which is a question for the embassy rather than an assumption.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: A few dozen programmes nationally, named rather than general. The UTokyo College of Design from September 2027; Waseda's six English-based schools; Keio's PEARL and GIGA; Sophia's Faculty of Liberal Arts; ICU's single bilingual liberal-arts degree; Tohoku's Future Global Leadership courses; Kyushu's international undergraduate programmes; Nagoya's G30; Tsukuba's Bachelor's Programme in Global Issues; Kyoto's iUP; APU's three colleges; and Akita International University, where every class is in English. Temple University Japan awards an American degree in Tokyo. A national total was not established.
language.englishProof: Set per programme. The University of Tokyo's College of Design requires one of its own designated tests from every applicant; Keio requires TOEFL iBT or IELTS Academic alongside the IB or SAT. Whether an IB English A or B result substitutes for a test is not established at either.
notes: Kyoto's iUP states that no Japanese proficiency is required at the outset — the six-month preparatory course exists to build it.

No English-taught programme requires Japanese to enrol, and essentially all of them require you to study it. You will need it for part-time work, housing and daily life whatever your degree is taught in.
APU and ICU are formally bilingual: you take courses in both languages as your Japanese improves.
MEXT's undergraduate scholarship runs the other way. Its default is a year of preparatory Japanese followed by a degree taught in Japanese.

feeContext.summary: Japan charges the same tuition to every nationality, so there is no EU/non-EU split to look for. The structure is a one-off admission fee plus annual tuition, with private universities well above national ones and science and engineering above the humanities. Budget for the admission fee separately: it is charged once and it is substantial.
feeContext.typicalRange: The University of Tokyo publishes an admission fee of 282,000 yen once and tuition of 642,960 yen a year — above the 535,800 yen national standard, which is why a national figure should never be quoted for a particular university. This is the only institutional figure read from an official page in this pass.
feeContext.priceYear: Not stated on the source page, read 2026-09-23

livingContext.housing: Most English-taught programmes guarantee or strongly prioritise a first-year place in a university dormitory or international house, which is cheaper and far simpler than the private market. APU houses all first-year international students in AP House. Private renting in Japan involves key money, guarantor requirements and agency fees that are difficult to navigate from abroad — take the dormitory.
livingContext.healthcare: Enrolment in National Health Insurance is compulsory for anyone staying more than three months and is arranged at the municipal office when you register. It covers roughly 70 per cent of medical costs and students typically add the university's own supplementary cover. A Danish EHIC does not apply.
livingContext.workRights: A student residence status permits part-time work only after obtaining Permission to Engage in Activity Other Than That Permitted, normally capped at 28 hours a week in term and longer in official holidays. Not re-verified from an official page in this pass — confirm with the Immigration Services Agency.
livingContext.residency: EU citizenship changes nothing. The university applies for a Certificate of Eligibility once you accept an offer; you take it to the Embassy of Japan in Copenhagen for a Student visa. On arrival you receive a residence card, register at the municipal office within 14 days and enrol in National Health Insurance. Allow three months and expect documents to need an apostille.
funding: MEXT Undergraduate Scholarship, Embassy Recommendation: in the 2027 round, five years from April 2027 to March 2032 including a preparatory year, 117,000 yen a month, entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees waived, and an economy air ticket each way. Applied for through the Japanese embassy between April and May of the year before arrival. Study is in Japanese unless MEXT directly places you at a university requiring none, and MEXT chooses the university.

University-recommendation MEXT places, under which a Japanese university nominates its own admitted students. The route exists and was not researched here; ask each admissions office whether it holds MEXT quota places.
JASSO Honors Scholarship, a monthly grant for privately financed international students. Amount not established here.

Institutional awards decided at admission. Waseda states that its scholarship recipients are determined by the admission result with no separate application and that its awards are grants rather than loans; APU operates tuition-reduction scholarships at several levels; Kyoto's iUP offers admission and tuition fee waivers plus monthly scholarships.
Danish SU follows separate rules for a full degree outside the EU/EEA. Check su.dk before assuming it travels with you.

sectorLandscape.summary: Japan's official answer to what its higher education is made of names five kinds of institution international students may enter, and English-language guidance almost always stops at the first. Beyond the 大学 sit 短期大学 junior colleges, 高等専門学校 kōsen that take students at fifteen for a five-year technical programme, 専門学校 professional training colleges, and since 2019 the 専門職大学 professional and vocational universities. The English-taught undergraduate sector is not one of these categories: it is a named set of programmes inside the first one, on a September or October intake that the rest of the system does not use.

routes.what: Four years to a bachelor's degree, six for medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine and pharmacy. National, local public and private, and the difference is largely money — the private universities charge considerably more and hold most of the English-taught provision. Every programme on this page sits here.
routes.note: The English-taught programmes inside this category are a named minority, admitted through their own rounds, on their own calendar, often at a different time of year from the Japanese-medium cohort at the same university.

routes.what: Two or three years ending in an associate degree rather than a bachelor's. Heavily weighted towards early-years and primary teaching, nursing and allied health, nutrition, home economics and design, and historically towards women students.
routes.note: Named because MEXT names it as one of the five routes open to international students. Whether any junior college admits an IB holder in practice, and in what language, was not established here.

routes.what: A five-year engineering and technology programme entered at fifteen, straight from lower secondary, with a two-year advanced course on top. Fifty-one national kōsen plus local public and private ones. Graduates are hired by Japanese manufacturers in numbers out of all proportion to the sector's size.
routes.note: Recorded because it has no European equivalent and because it is invisible in English-language advice. An IB Diploma holder is four years too late for the ordinary entry point; the advanced course and third-year transfer are the routes that could theoretically apply, and neither was researched.

routes.what: Post-secondary specialised training: two-year diploma courses of 62 credits or more and four-year advanced diploma courses of 124 or more, in animation and game design, IT, hospitality and cookery, fashion, care work, automotive engineering and dozens of other named trades.
routes.note: This is Japan's answer to the question this project asks of every country: the institution type nobody mentions to foreigners. It is the largest part of Japanese post-secondary education by student numbers after the universities, it enrols a great many international students, and it is essentially absent from English-language guidance for IB students. Not researched here beyond MEXT's own description of it.

routes.what: Created in 2019 to sit between the university and the professional training college: four years to a bachelor's degree (professional), or two to three years to an associate degree (professional), with a substantial compulsory placement built into the curriculum.
routes.note: The newest category in the Japanese system and the least documented in English. Recorded because it exists and because a route omitted is a route invisible.

routes.englishName: Japan campus of a foreign university
routes.what: A foreign university operating in Japan and awarding its own home degree. Temple University, Japan Campus is the oldest and largest, teaching entirely in English in Tokyo and allowing transfer to Philadelphia.
routes.note: Useful if you want an American-style degree with a Japanese life around it, and priced accordingly — it charges American tuition, not Japanese.

notes: Written after the four other floor checks were already true. Four institutions were read for their own dates — the University of Tokyo, Keio, Waseda and Kyoto — out of the fifteen on the Japanese profile. The other eleven are listed and unread, and their rounds will differ.
Re-check in November 2026, when Waseda is expected to publish its September 2027 window, and again in April 2027 for the MEXT 2028 guidelines.

Not established: the Kyoto iUP closing date, which sits inside a guidelines document rather than on the site; any published minimum IB score anywhere; the application fees; the JASSO Honors Scholarship amount; and the university-recommendation route into MEXT.

Not established, and the largest gap: the Danish MEXT application dates. The Embassy of Japan in Denmark's own pages refused every request on 2026-09-23 with an edge-network 403, and MEXT states that the schedule is the embassy's to set. That is a telephone call, not another fetch.
